name: capell-app/inertia
description: Server side of a Vue or React front end for Capell pages, with a root view allow-list and a Diagnostics health check.

healthChecks.label: Capell Inertia runtime bridge is installed and configured.

marketplace.summary: Hands Capell page content to a Vue or React front end, with an adapter setting, a root view allow-list and a Diagnostics check.
marketplace.description: Teams building the public site in Vue or React get each page with its title, content, meta tags, language and layout containers. Choose Vue or React with one environment setting, limit which HTML shells can be used, and confirm the setup from a Diagnostics check.
marketplace.problem: We build our front end in Vue or React and have no way to serve Capell pages through it.
marketplace.outcome: Capell pages reach your Vue or React front end while editors stay in the admin.

faq.question: Will editors notice anything different in the admin?
faq.answer: No. Editors keep working in the Capell admin and see nothing different. Only the way pages reach visitors changes, so they arrive through your Vue or React front end.

faq.question: What do I need besides this package?
faq.answer: One adapter, either the Vue adapter or the React adapter, a theme set up to show pages through Inertia, and your own front-end build. The package itself contains no JavaScript.

faq.question: Which should I choose, Vue or React?
faq.answer: Vue is the default. A React site changes one setting to react and installs the React adapter instead.

faq.question: Which widgets come with a component for my front end?
faq.answer: Content, image and title widgets each carry a component name for the front end to use. Other widget types carry none.
